result.title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
result.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, Accepted by Medical Image Analysis
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

AI.brief_summary: SurgPace 提出面向手术多模态大模型的多复杂度感知渐进蒸馏框架：用预测置信度与 Lorentz 几何一致性估计样本难度，驱动由易到难的连续课程，并在特征、logit、概率三层对齐师生表示，逐步将训练重心从教师模仿转向任务监督，以得到紧凑、低显存的手术 MLLM。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文本身不研究 latent 视觉推理，但其按样本难度调度监督强度、在多层内部表示上对齐师生状态、并随训练阶段转移监督目标的思路，可能为 LVR 的训练监督分配与潜在状态对齐提供可核查线索。
